## How it works

- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation states that medications, toxins or other neurological conditions can cause secondary parkinsonism. (low confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/what-is-parkinsons/types-parkinsonisms

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] NINDS describes Parkinson’s disease as a progressive nervous-system disorder involving nerve-cell damage and death; WHO also describes worsening over time. (medium confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape · also: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease
- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation distinguishes parkinsonism, a set of movement symptoms, from a specific diagnosis; the MDS criteria separately assess whether Parkinson’s disease is its cause. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/what-is-parkinsons/types-parkinsonisms · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474316/
- [statement] For determining Parkinson’s disease as the cause of parkinsonism, the MDS criteria use absolute exclusions, red flags counterbalanced by supportive criteria, and supportive features. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474316/
- [statement] The MDS criteria distinguish clinically established Parkinson’s disease, prioritizing specificity, from probable disease, balancing sensitivity and specificity. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474316/
- [statement] WHO and NINDS describe non-motor involvement in Parkinson’s disease, including mental-health and sleep problems. (medium confidence) — https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape · also: https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease, https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease
- [statement] NINDS notes that some people with Parkinson’s disease never develop tremor. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease
- [statement] NINDS states that no specific single test can definitively diagnose Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease
- [statement] NINDS states that a dopamine transporter scan cannot distinguish Parkinson’s disease from atypical parkinsonism; Beach and Adler likewise describe dopamine functional scans as lacking specificity for Parkinson’s disease. (medium confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6544441/
- [statement] WHO reported that global estimates for 2019 showed over 8.5 million individuals with Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-08-09) — https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Beach and Adler report that autopsy-validated studies found misdiagnosis common in early clinically diagnosed Parkinson’s disease compared with patients followed for years. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6544441/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The MDS clinical diagnostic criteria define motor parkinsonism as bradykinesia plus rest tremor or rigidity. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474316/
- [statement] WHO reports gaps in medication and surgical-resource accessibility, availability and affordability, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-08-09) — https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease
